Every seg carrying source="urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:amidah/hodaah/modim" now has content, so URN scope rule 1 is satisfied. The old <tei:seg …/> with no content is gone.

Resolved scopes under rules 2 and 3: …/modim/modim runs from its milestone to the modim_end milestone, the next milestone of the same unit, and so ends at לָךְ. …/modim/modim_end runs from וְעַל through the pb and נִסֶּיךָ… to קִוִּינוּ לָךְ: and is closed by the bare terminator. The pb is a different unit and ends neither scope. Neither scope now ends on a dangling וְעַל. The second scope opens with a complete clause, וְעַל נִסֶּיךָ שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם עִמָּנוּ, which answers the prior 'split in the middle of a phrase' finding. Each milestone sits before its seg, per 'place its milestone before the semantic span'.

Placement on the source: s154-row8, right column, last line ends הַפְּקוּדוֹת לָךְ וְעַל, and s155-row2 line 1 begins נִסֶּיךָ. So וְעַל is printed on 154 and belongs before pb 66, as encoded. No letters are omitted or repeated. The before/after concatenation of the three fragments is identical apart from the boundary move and the separate שֶׁבְּכָל־עֵת maqaf change. The left column on s154-row8 (Modim deRabbanan, ending בָּרוּךְ אֵל הַהוֹדָאוֹת:) is not in this unit.

The documentary order requires both contexts. In the prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he running order, one context transcludes …/hodaah/modim/modim, then …/hodaah/modim_derabbanan, then …/hodaah/modim/modim_end. Another context transcludes modim_derabbanan, modim/modim_end, then hodaah/tail. This matches the right column / left column / right-column continuation layout across 154–155. Both URMs are actual transclusion targets, so collapsing to one milestone (the prior suggestion, made without this order evidence) would break the edition order. Both URMs keep their existing values.

In machzor_expanded-opensiddur-he, the transclusion is the whole div …/hodaah/modim, followed by modim_derabbanan and tail. That yields the continuous text מוֹדִים … לָךְ וְעַל נִסֶּיךָ … לָךְ: with no break, and the boundary move does not affect it.

The prior condition 'only justified if the English body carries the same …/modim_end boundary' does not apply. No EN counterpart exists in the data or the project, and the boundary is justified by the documentary order instead. The Alignment section only governs joins between texts that both carry the URN.

Paragraph and page structure: one tei:p, unchanged, spans pb 65 (div facs n153) and pb 66 (n154), and the closing terminator is present. The maqaf placement is consistent with the image: s155-row2 line 1 ends שֶׁבְּכָל־ at the line end, continuing with עֵת, and the XML has שֶׁבְּכָל־עֵת. The earlier שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם on the same line has no maqaf, and the XML has none. That is placement only, not certification of the glyph.

Local scope: …/hodaah/tail/veall_kullam is a prayer-part milestone. It is followed by seg source="urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:amidah/hodaah/veal_kullam" holding וְעַל־כֻּלָּם … לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד: and then a bare prayer-part terminator, so the local scope is exactly that sentence. ukhetov and vekhol_hachayyim follow the same pattern, each in its own tei:p with its own terminator. vekhol_hachayyim's seg source is amidah/hodaah/hatov_shimkha.

Canonical bounded source: each canonical URN is on a seg with content, so it references exactly that content (rule 1). The local corresp and the canonical seg@source are different kinds of identity: the local occurrence URN against the reusable prayer URN. No quoted guideline requires them to share a slug, and 'Do not duplicate a canonical URN merely because the text is printed again elsewhere' is satisfied by using the canonical URN as the source rather than as the corresp. The spelling difference veall_kullam/veal_kullam is therefore not a violation, and renaming existing IDs is not called for.

Hebrew-only: there is no EN body and none was invented, so the prior 'acceptable if the English body uses the identical local URN' condition has nothing to apply to. Any future EN must reuse the existing local corresp values (…/tail/veall_kullam, …/tail/ukhetov, …/tail/vekhol_hachayyim) to align, per Alignment ('The join is on exact URN equality').
